sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Salvadora persica is an evergreen, many-branched shrub or small tree of dry and often saline regions, reaching about 7 m. Its broad crown carries fleshy, oval to nearly round leaves; the illustration shows the rounded foliage and fruit.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Small yellowish flowers form slender branched clusters. The fleshy, spherical fruits are about 5–10 mm across and ripen from red toward dark tones.

sections.title: Uses and edibility
sections.text: Twigs and roots are traditionally used as miswak chewing sticks for cleaning teeth. A regional landscape guide describes the ripe fruit as edible; the plant is not interchangeable with other species when identifying food plants.
